Car theft Con - Nicky Troll

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
these car thieves are so good, victims willing hand over their keys without even being threatened

Summary:
These criminals are higher grade! They passed their car thief training with top marks!

Instead of putting a gun in the victim's face and using violence and intimidation to get the car - they pose as dealership employees - victims hand over the keys and only figure out hours, if not days later that they were conned. The car thieves made off with the car with the key and a head start without any cops chasing them - the car is gone for good!


Further information:
From my hijack story we learnt that criminals need to modify their MO's to get the keys from the driver because newer cars can't be stolen and jippo-ed to start. But instead of using violence and hijacking, some car thieves are using more civilised methods.

MODUS OPERANDI
Crooks scout manufacturer Facebook pages for complaints from car owners - they respond to them offering to fix the problem or a complementary service and even offer to collect the car from the car owner. Once they collect the car, they're off with the keys and at least a couple of hours to get out the tracking device.

CASE STUDY 1
A lady complained about the service at Mercedes, she collected her new car and they didn't even put a ribbon on it... yada, yada, yada... the crooks contacted her - saying they would like to make up for the dissatisfying service and would like to offer her a full tank of petrol and free smash and grab film, along with a special anti-chip coat for her car. She was very happy with the freebies and even more please that they dealership would come and collect her car and then deliver it later in the afternoon. Her car was never returned!

CASE STUDY 2
A man complained on the Landrover page about his sunroof that was giving problems. He also received call, the "dealership" came to collect and that was the last time he saw his car.

HOW TO DO IT
We post on a manufacturer page complaining and wait to see if they take the bait - I know it's a long shot - but it could work - that's how I caught my online dating crooks with a fake profile :)

I will have access to industry insiders - just waiting for details on their involvement - but if you're keen - I can post my "complaint" ASAP.

This is a syndicate operating, there have been arrests - previously they used an insider at the service departments and would call the dealership saying a driver was going to collect the car - the dealership would hand over the car and keys to the so-called driver and the car would be gone by the time the real owner arrived to collect. They've now modified the scam and are targeting complainants on Facebook.

Script:


FINAL SCRIPT CAR THIEVES 2.0

VO: Gone are the days of dodgy car thieves stealing your wheels, on the side of the road, with minimal skill and basic tools.

LINK: But today criminals are cracking intricate security system and running elaborate cons – taking a car from its owner with no violence, no damage in just seconds.

THIEF: It;s easy now, going to pick up a car, you get the key and you go with the car.

VO: A convicted car thief spoke to us on condition that he did not appear on camera – this is his voice, but the person in our visuals is an actor.

In his 14-year criminal career, he says this MO, is by far, the cleverest.

These car thieves don’t physically rob you – they are con-artists. At first, they stole cars by tricking vehicle service providers into thinking they were the owners of luxury vehicles and that their so-called driver would collect the car.

THIEF: I come and speak to the people of the dealership and says, so and so send me to get the car // They just accept it – I don't know why

VO: The kingpin would set everything up beforehand, spinning stories about lost cellphones and new contact details.

THIEF: No one asks you questions and too much things they just give you the car, it like they have a connection or something – you can’t just come and fetch a car like that, you understand.

VO: It’s whole a new dimension to vehicle theft – having analysed 45 cases totaling R30 million, South African Insurance Crime Bureau’s Senior Project Manager, Lieb Liebenberg says as businesses wised up to the con, the criminals evolved the MO.

LIEB: They changed to targeting the public in a reversed role where they will pretend to be the service provider.

VO: In May this year, Lefu Mohloki had problems with his Range Rover after a service at the Midrand dealership.

He took to social media to complain and contacted Land Rover SA. After a call from a so-called customer services manager, Lefu’s car was to be collected, repaired with 24 hours and returned to his house.

This call is from the man claiming he was from Land Rover SA confirming the collection:


UPSOUND CALL: We spoke to your wife, will be at the dealership shortly

LEFU: He knew everything about me, he name dropped Bongani, my service advisor, he knew the problems that the vehicle had, it was very convincing, for me it was a person from Land Rover SA

VO: But it wasn’t – Lefu’s car wasn’t headed to any Land Rover Dealership for repairs – the car had been stolen.

Land Rover South Africa’s Rory Beattie says they are aware of this new trend in vehicle theft.

DEREK: Rory, The concern is that in many cases the criminals had information that had to come from the dealership
RORY: not necessarily, we all need to mindful and cognizant of the environment we live in the ability to get that information of numerous sources off the internet – while we’ve done internal investigations there’s been nothing that suggest any level of inside work going on within our network.

VO: Although Lefu revealed some of the details of his case on a consumer complaints website, he is adamant there was more to it.

LEFU: For me it’s very clear, it’s an inside job at the dealership itself because they knew the nitty gritty of the vehicle, they knew everything, addresses, names, that kind of stuff – it’s through and through the dealership

VO: But it’s not just Land Rover that is being targeted. Most luxury cars are on the king pin’s list.

THIEF: Expensive cars, he goes for big things not the small cars. Merc Big Badge goes for R30 000 also, you get a R10 000 there, they take R20 000 – Land Rovers, the new ones? They also go R30 000, R35000.

VO: Of the 30 cars taken this year, Land Rover tops the list with 15 vehicles, followed by Mercedes Benz with 9. No two cases were from the same service provider or dealership.

The only connection it seems is the centralized data systems used by manufacturers to store service histories and customer details. Could the information have come from someone inside a dealership with access to these systems?

LINK: A recent study showed that organisations often focus on external threats, like hackers, but they appear to be overlooking the threat from within the business.

VO: CSIR Senior Researcher, Ignus Swart deals with cybercrime investigations.

IGNUS: right now in the security chain the human is the weakest link. There are strong technical controls if properly implemented, but the people are the ones that are actually failing at this point and time.

VO: Our source tells us, that sometimes the thieves access client info by going to dealerships and posing as potential buyers – fishing for private client info that could lead them straight to a car they’re hoping to steal.

Could it be as simple as just asking for information at any branch?

We went undercover to two randomly selected dealerships to test this theory.

At Land Rover the sales agent even flipped the screen to reveal the details.

UNDERCOVER UPSOUND LANDROVER: …Bram Fisher Drive, Randburg…

VO: At Mercedes Benz they also revealed an address.

UNDERCOVER UPSOUND MERCEDES: Wat’s die adres? 235 drive, Montana.

VO: Despite, the fact that third party personal information was disclosed to our operative in both stings, both manufacturers insisted that their systems are adequate.

Mayur Bhana is from Mercedes Benz South Africa.

MAYUR: The processes we have are sound, the example you have brought to my attention where you got customer data randomly going to a dealership, giving a registration number, I am not sure of the context.
DEREK: But is shouldn’t happen.
MAYUR: that information should not be passed.

VO: While Mercedes conceded that there could be possible problems, Land Rover were less willing to budge.

DEREK So it shows you that the system isn’t water tight at this stage?
RORY: I think it’s as water tight as we can make it and we are in line with every legislative requirement // the criminal mind and how they coerce information from someone that I can’t comment on and how that is done.
DEREK: I just want to point out it wasn’t really a criminal mind, it was a woman walking in and saying can I have details about this vehicle.

VO: The reality is that is that the information could have landed in the wrong hands - putting the owners at risk of being robbed or attacked in their own homes.

LINK: Now, there’s POPI the new Protection of Personal Information Act - Big business will have to shape up on personal data security or they could face up to R10 million in fines, or even up to 10 years behind bars.

IGNUS: It’s a law, the enforcement of the law is the most important part of it.

VO: Legal expert Pamela Stein says these types of leaks are inexcusable.

Pamela: That would be an absolute breach of our data protection law, you can not disclose information like that to third parties, certainly without the permission of the data subject and in those circumstances it would be breach.

VO: A breach that cost Jacqui Biscardi her new Mercedes Benz GLA. Picking up her dream car kick started a nightmare journey.

JACQUI: the car was still parked in the parking lot, it had a lot of dust on it //
DEREK: no red ribbon?
JACQUI: nothing... that’s what I you, I expect fireworks at least – it was quite disappointing.

LINK: Jacqui drove away in her brand new GLA, but she was so upset about her handover that she made a call to Merc’s head office

VO: SHE ALSO POSTED ON FACEBOOK: The dealership sent Flowers, chocolates and offered a free AMG race day as an apology, but there was more to come – she got a call from a so-called Merc SA MD.

JACQUI: Calvin strung me onto this wonderful story of him coming to collect my vehicle to do free glazing on it and on the way back they would fill up my car with some diesel to try and make me a happy customer
DEREK: did Calvin sound very convincing?
JACQUI: Just the way he knew my story// there wasn’t any little red flag that made me think, hey? I’m... this is a bit of a scam kind of thing.

VO: The driver wore a Mercedes shirt and a name badge, so Jacqui felt confident that he was the real deal.

JACQUI: on the way out, he stopped and opened the window and said, bye Mrs. Biscardi, don’t worry everything is fine. And I waved and smiled and there went my GLA...

VO: The criminals have a head start, with the victims only realizing hours later they’ve been conned and the car is gone.

LIEB: WE must consider the time factor // in these cases, the vehicle can already be in Botswana before it’s realised that this vehicle actually was stolen through a scam and in that time the tracking devices unfortunately can be removed.

VO: Jacqui’s tracking unit was discovered along the freeway to Soweto with no sign of her GLA.

Mercedes–Benz South Africa says the investigation is ongoing and they are cooperating with the police.

MAYUR: It is an assumption at this time that the information is coming from within our origanisation at this time.// in this case, it is very difficult to understand how these perpurtrators are getting hold of our information // if any / if any.

VO: Subsequently a suspect was arrested. He had Mercedes Benz uniforms at his home – which may have been used in cases like Jacqui’s.

Shortly afterwards, Jacqui and her husband Tony received this call from a man claiming to be in charge:

UPSOUND CALL: …is the car worth your life?

VO: The voice has been identified as that of Jermaine Prim – a man serving a six-year sentence for car theft at the Diepkloof prison.

Our Car thief insider, says Jermaine is the king pin.

THIEF: If he tells you something, you know he’s telling the truth you’ll get it right. He’s very clever That man, he’s very clever!

VO: Lefu agrees, this isn’t the work of an amateur.

LEFU: if the insurance didn’t pay out I would be sitting with R900 thousand debt to pay for a vehicle, no car to show for it. I mean these people are very, they are too clever, they’re precise.

VO: And with Jermaine Prim due for release in February next year, boom time is coming.

THIEF: when if he’s doing it like from prison now, and he’s making money from prison, so if he’s outside it’s going to be worse mos



PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: Car thieves using clever cons get vehicle owners to hand over their car keys.

JACQUI: he said, bye Mrs. Biscardi, don’t worry everything is fine. And I waved and smiled and there went my GLA...

PROMO 2
VO: Are u savvy enough to spot the Syndicates Stealing cars through sophisticated cons, making off with luxury vehicles in seconds?

THIEF: It;s easy now, going to pick up a car, you get the key and you go with the car.

VO: Carte Blanche exposes a brand new car scam.

Amalia Christoforou Managing Editor [t] +27 11 886 8899 [c] +27 83 700 3475 [f] +27 86 508 3284 www.carteblanche.co.za Insert Details Presenter: Derek Watts Voice-over Presenter: Devi Sankaree Govender Camera: Willem Pretorius Offline editor: Jan Potgieter Online editor: Jan Potgieter Audio final mix: Floris Brand Booked Footage Footage returned: No Footage Declaration I confirm that all footage agreements have been signed and submitted via Jotform: No Music Cue Sheet Music Title Type Track Number Duration Publisher Composer Record/CD Number NOBLE ARTS PULSE Background 8 00:00:24 Extreme MEL WESSON DCD 049 THE RIOT ACT Background 47 00:00:54 Extreme TILLMAN/VEDIK DCD 034 MOTIONAL RESCUE Background 16 00:01:02 Extreme MEL WESSON DCD 049 CULTURE SHOCK Background 19 00:00:24 Extreme Mel Wesson DCD 037 CULTURE SHOCK Background 4 00:00:36 Extreme Mel Wesson DCD 037 MOVING TARGET Background 28 00:01:02 Extreme Mel Wesson DCD 037 DEEP INDEX Background 11 00:00:27 Extreme Mel Wesson DCD 049 TX Details Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 04 January 2015 - Carte Blanche HD Nikola Vrahimis 24 March 2015 Script: FINAL SCRIPT CAR THIEVES 2.0 VO: Gone are the days of dodgy car thieves stealing your wheels, on the side of the road, with minimal skill and basic tools. LINK: But today criminals are cracking intricate security system and running elaborate cons – taking a car from its owner with no violence, no damage in just seconds. THIEF: It;s easy now, going to pick up a car, you get the key and you go with the car. VO: A convicted car thief spoke to us on condition that he did not appear on camera – this is his voice, but the person in our visuals is an actor. In his 14-year criminal career, he says this MO, is by far, the cleverest. These car thieves don’t physically rob you – they are con-artists. At first, they stole cars by tricking vehicle service providers into thinking they were the owners of luxury vehicles and that their so-called driver would collect the car. THIEF: I come and speak to the people of the dealership and says, so and so send me to get the car // They just accept it – I don't know why VO: The kingpin would set everything up beforehand, spinning stories about lost cellphones and new contact details. THIEF: No one asks you questions and too much things they just give you the car, it like they have a connection or something – you can’t just come and fetch a car like that, you understand. VO: It’s whole a new dimension to vehicle theft – having analysed 45 cases totaling R30 million, South African Insurance Crime Bureau’s Senior Project Manager, Lieb Liebenberg says as businesses wised up to the con, the criminals evolved the MO. LIEB: They changed to targeting the public in a reversed role where they will pretend to be the service provider. VO: In May this year, Lefu Mohloki had problems with his Range Rover after a service at the Midrand dealership. He took to social media to complain and contacted Land Rover SA. After a call from a so-called customer services manager, Lefu’s car was to be collected, repaired with 24 hours and returned to his house. This call is from the man claiming he was from Land Rover SA confirming the collection: UPSOUND CALL: We spoke to your wife, will be at the dealership shortly LEFU: He knew everything about me, he name dropped Bongani, my service advisor, he knew the problems that the vehicle had, it was very convincing, for me it was a person from Land Rover SA VO: But it wasn’t – Lefu’s car wasn’t headed to any Land Rover Dealership for repairs – the car had been stolen. Land Rover South Africa’s Rory Beattie says they are aware of this new trend in vehicle theft. DEREK: Rory, The concern is that in many cases the criminals had information that had to come from the dealership RORY: not necessarily, we all need to mindful and cognizant of the environment we live in the ability to get that information of numerous sources off the internet – while we’ve done internal investigations there’s been nothing that suggest any level of inside work going on within our network. VO: Although Lefu revealed some of the details of his case on a consumer complaints website, he is adamant there was more to it. LEFU: For me it’s very clear, it’s an inside job at the dealership itself because they knew the nitty gritty of the vehicle, they knew everything, addresses, names, that kind of stuff – it’s through and through the dealership VO: But it’s not just Land Rover that is being targeted. Most luxury cars are on the king pin’s list. THIEF: Expensive cars, he goes for big things not the small cars. Merc Big Badge goes for R30 000 also, you get a R10 000 there, they take R20 000 – Land Rovers, the new ones? They also go R30 000, R35000. VO: Of the 30 cars taken this year, Land Rover tops the list with 15 vehicles, followed by Mercedes Benz with 9. No two cases were from the same service provider or dealership. The only connection it seems is the centralized data systems used by manufacturers to store service histories and customer details. Could the information have come from someone inside a dealership with access to these systems? LINK: A recent study showed that organisations often focus on external threats, like hackers, but they appear to be overlooking the threat from within the business. VO: CSIR Senior Researcher, Ignus Swart deals with cybercrime investigations. IGNUS: right now in the security chain the human is the weakest link. There are strong technical controls if properly implemented, but the people are the ones that are actually failing at this point and time. VO: Our source tells us, that sometimes the thieves access client info by going to dealerships and posing as potential buyers – fishing for private client info that could lead them straight to a car they’re hoping to steal. Could it be as simple as just asking for information at any branch? We went undercover to two randomly selected dealerships to test this theory. At Land Rover the sales agent even flipped the screen to reveal the details. UNDERCOVER UPSOUND LANDROVER: …Bram Fisher Drive, Randburg… VO: At Mercedes Benz they also revealed an address. UNDERCOVER UPSOUND MERCEDES: Wat’s die adres? 235 drive, Montana. VO: Despite, the fact that third party personal information was disclosed to our operative in both stings, both manufacturers insisted that their systems are adequate. Mayur Bhana is from Mercedes Benz South Africa. MAYUR: The processes we have are sound, the example you have brought to my attention where you got customer data randomly going to a dealership, giving a registration number, I am not sure of the context. DEREK: But is shouldn’t happen. MAYUR: that information should not be passed. VO: While Mercedes conceded that there could be possible problems, Land Rover were less willing to budge. DEREK So it shows you that the system isn’t water tight at this stage? RORY: I think it’s as water tight as we can make it and we are in line with every legislative requirement // the criminal mind and how they coerce information from someone that I can’t comment on and how that is done. DEREK: I just want to point out it wasn’t really a criminal mind, it was a woman walking in and saying can I have details about this vehicle. VO: The reality is that is that the information could have landed in the wrong hands - putting the owners at risk of being robbed or attacked in their own homes. LINK: Now, there’s POPI the new Protection of Personal Information Act - Big business will have to shape up on personal data security or they could face up to R10 million in fines, or even up to 10 years behind bars. IGNUS: It’s a law, the enforcement of the law is the most important part of it. VO: Legal expert Pamela Stein says these types of leaks are inexcusable. Pamela: That would be an absolute breach of our data protection law, you can not disclose information like that to third parties, certainly without the permission of the data subject and in those circumstances it would be breach. VO: A breach that cost Jacqui Biscardi her new Mercedes Benz GLA. Picking up her dream car kick started a nightmare journey. JACQUI: the car was still parked in the parking lot, it had a lot of dust on it // DEREK: no red ribbon? JACQUI: nothing... that’s what I you, I expect fireworks at least – it was quite disappointing. LINK: Jacqui drove away in her brand new GLA, but she was so upset about her handover that she made a call to Merc’s head office VO: SHE ALSO POSTED ON FACEBOOK: The dealership sent Flowers, chocolates and offered a free AMG race day as an apology, but there was more to come – she got a call from a so-called Merc SA MD. JACQUI: Calvin strung me onto this wonderful story of him coming to collect my vehicle to do free glazing on it and on the way back they would fill up my car with some diesel to try and make me a happy customer DEREK: did Calvin sound very convincing? JACQUI: Just the way he knew my story// there wasn’t any little red flag that made me think, hey? I’m... this is a bit of a scam kind of thing. VO: The driver wore a Mercedes shirt and a name badge, so Jacqui felt confident that he was the real deal. JACQUI: on the way out, he stopped and opened the window and said, bye Mrs. Biscardi, don’t worry everything is fine. And I waved and smiled and there went my GLA... VO: The criminals have a head start, with the victims only realizing hours later they’ve been conned and the car is gone. LIEB: WE must consider the time factor // in these cases, the vehicle can already be in Botswana before it’s realised that this vehicle actually was stolen through a scam and in that time the tracking devices unfortunately can be removed. VO: Jacqui’s tracking unit was discovered along the freeway to Soweto with no sign of her GLA. Mercedes–Benz South Africa says the investigation is ongoing and they are cooperating with the police. MAYUR: It is an assumption at this time that the information is coming from within our origanisation at this time.// in this case, it is very difficult to understand how these perpurtrators are getting hold of our information // if any / if any. VO: Subsequently a suspect was arrested. He had Mercedes Benz uniforms at his home – which may have been used in cases like Jacqui’s. Shortly afterwards, Jacqui and her husband Tony received this call from a man claiming to be in charge: UPSOUND CALL: …is the car worth your life? VO: The voice has been identified as that of Jermaine Prim – a man serving a six-year sentence for car theft at the Diepkloof prison. Our Car thief insider, says Jermaine is the king pin. THIEF: If he tells you something, you know he’s telling the truth you’ll get it right. He’s very clever That man, he’s very clever! VO: Lefu agrees, this isn’t the work of an amateur. LEFU: if the insurance didn’t pay out I would be sitting with R900 thousand debt to pay for a vehicle, no car to show for it. I mean these people are very, they are too clever, they’re precise. VO: And with Jermaine Prim due for release in February next year, boom time is coming. THIEF: when if he’s doing it like from prison now, and he’s making money from prison, so if he’s outside it’s going to be worse mos PROMOS PROMO 1 VO: Car thieves using clever cons get vehicle owners to hand over their car keys. JACQUI: he said, bye Mrs. Biscardi, don’t worry everything is fine. And I waved and smiled and there went my GLA... PROMO 2 VO: Are u savvy enough to spot the Syndicates Stealing cars through sophisticated cons, making off with luxury vehicles in seconds? THIEF: It;s easy now, going to pick up a car, you get the key and you go with the car. VO: Carte Blanche exposes a brand new car scam.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): these car thieves are so good, victims willing hand over their keys without even being threatened
metadata.Summary: These criminals are higher grade! They passed their car thief training with top marks! Instead of putting a gun in the victim's face and using violence and intimidation to get the car - they pose as dealership employees - victims hand over the keys and only figure out hours, if not days later that they were conned. The car thieves made off with the car with the key and a head start without any cops chasing them - the car is gone for good!
metadata.Further information: From my hijack story we learnt that criminals need to modify their MO's to get the keys from the driver because newer cars can't be stolen and jippo-ed to start. But instead of using violence and hijacking, some car thieves are using more civilised methods. MODUS OPERANDI Crooks scout manufacturer Facebook pages for complaints from car owners - they respond to them offering to fix the problem or a complementary service and even offer to collect the car from the car owner. Once they collect the car, they're off with the keys and at least a couple of hours to get out the tracking device. CASE STUDY 1 A lady complained about the service at Mercedes, she collected her new car and they didn't even put a ribbon on it... yada, yada, yada... the crooks contacted her - saying they would like to make up for the dissatisfying service and would like to offer her a full tank of petrol and free smash and grab film, along with a special anti-chip coat for her car. She was very happy with the freebies and even more please that they dealership would come and collect her car and then deliver it later in the afternoon. Her car was never returned! CASE STUDY 2 A man complained on the Landrover page about his sunroof that was giving problems. He also received call, the "dealership" came to collect and that was the last time he saw his car. HOW TO DO IT We post on a manufacturer page complaining and wait to see if they take the bait - I know it's a long shot - but it could work - that's how I caught my online dating crooks with a fake profile :) I will have access to industry insiders - just waiting for details on their involvement - but if you're keen - I can post my "complaint" ASAP. This is a syndicate operating, there have been arrests - previously they used an insider at the service departments and would call the dealership saying a driver was going to collect the car - the dealership would hand over the car and keys to the so-called driver and the car would be gone by the time the real owner arrived to collect. They've now modified the scam and are targeting complainants on Facebook.
